definitions.explanation: A tool used to remove corks from wine bottles. The ～抜き pattern (remover/opener) is productive in Japanese.

examples.japanese: コルク{抜|ぬ}きを{貸|か}してください。
コルク{抜|ぬ}きが{見|み}つからなくて、ワインが{開|あ}けられない。
examples.english: I can't find the corkscrew, so I can't open the wine.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}{先|さき}でワインを{買|か}ったが、コルク{抜|ぬ}きを{持|も}ってくるのを{忘|わす}れてしまった。
examples.english: I bought wine at the travel destination, but I forgot to bring a corkscrew.

notes:
USAGE:
Follows the productive pattern of ～{抜|ぬ}き (remover/opener), seen also in {栓|せん}{抜|ぬ}き (bottle opener) and {釘|くぎ}{抜|ぬ}き (nail puller). Also called ワインオープナー.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- コルク{抜|ぬ}きでワインを{開|あ}ける (to open wine with a corkscrew)
- コルク{抜|ぬ}きを{使|つか}う (to use a corkscrew)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {栓|せん}{抜|ぬ}き: bottle opener — for prying off bottle caps
- ワインオープナー: wine opener — a loanword alternative
